function.name: get_deploy_target
function.description: Read how a repository ships to an environment: provider, variables, health URL, and the deploy recipe rendered with those values.

env.description: stage | preprod | prod. Omit to list every configured environment.

repository_id.description: Repository UUID (the repository_id in your task snapshot). Omit to use the repository of the task this run is working on.

function.name: get_incident
function.description: Read one production incident in full: raw alert payload, timeline, occurrence count and the current remedy hypothesis. Call this first when working an incident task.

incident_id.description: Incident UUID (it is printed in the task description)

function.name: list_deploy_templates
function.description: List the available deploy recipes (GCP Cloud Run/GKE, AWS ECS/Lambda, Vercel, Fly). Use one of these instead of inventing a deploy workflow.

kind.description: Repo kind filter: backend | frontend | mobile | worker | monorepo

function.name: list_incidents
function.description: List production incidents. Use it to see what is currently broken in an environment before starting work.

repository_id.description: Repository UUID (the repository_id in your task snapshot) to list one repository's incidents. Omit to list incidents across every repository.

status.description: Comma-separated statuses (open,triaging,proposed,fixing). Defaults to everything still live.

function.name: load_deploy_template
function.description: Load a deploy recipe in full: the workflow YAML to write, the secrets it needs, the smoke check and the rollback. Follow it instead of writing a deploy from memory.

function.name: propose_incident_remedy
function.description: Record the fix you concluded for an incident: what broke and exactly what to do about it. Under the suggest policy this is the deliverable — do not change production code, write the proposal here and let the human decide.

evidence.description: Facts that support the diagnosis (log lines, deploy times, metrics)

rollback.description: True when the remedy is to redeploy the last good release

steps.description: Concrete, executable steps (commands, files, config keys)

summary.description: One paragraph: root cause and the fix

function.name: record_local_deploy
function.description: Record a deploy you ran from this machine (the repo's scripts/release-local.sh or scripts/deploy-local.sh) so it appears in Operations → Changes next to the GitHub Actions ones. Call it TWICE per deploy: once before the script with status=in_progress, then once after it with status=completed and the conclusion, passing back the run_id the first call returned. This records only — it never deploys anything.

command.description: What you ran, e.g. 'bash scripts/release-local.sh web'

conclusion.description: success | failure | cancelled. Required when status is completed; a failed script is reported as failure, not left unreported.

env.description: stage | preprod | prod — the environment the script actually deployed to

head_ref.description: Branch or ref that was built (usually main)

head_sha.description: Commit that was built — `git rev-parse origin/main`, since the scripts build origin/main, not the working tree.

repository_id.description: Repository UUID from your task snapshot. Omit to use the repository this run is working in.

run_id.description: The run_id the in_progress call returned. Required by the completed call, omitted by the first one.

status.description: in_progress before the script runs, completed after it

function.name: resolve_incident
function.description: Close an incident once production is verified healthy again. Only call this after checking the environment, not after merely shipping a fix.

note.description: What fixed it and how recovery was verified

function.name: update_deploy_target
function.description: Record where an environment actually answers (base URL / health URL / logs URL) after a deploy — keep deploy targets truthful. It writes nothing else: provider, template and variables stay as the human configured them.

app_url.description: Where this environment's installable mobile build currently lives (the APK the pipeline published). QA installs from it onto the test device. Omit to leave it as it is. The package name itself is set by a human and cannot be changed here.

base_url.description: Where the environment answers, from the deploy output (e.g. https://api-stage.example.com). Omit to leave it as it is.

health_url.description: The URL the production monitor should poll (e.g. https://api-stage.example.com/health). Omit to leave it as it is.

logs_url.description: An endpoint THIS APPLICATION serves that returns its recent logs (e.g. https://api-stage.example.com/internal/logs). get_deploy_logs reads it after a deploy, which is how a deploy that came up but is logging errors gets noticed — health_url only ever answers "it is up". Record it only if the app actually exposes such a route; do not invent one, and do not point it at a cloud provider's log console. Omit to leave it as it is.

repository_id.description: Repository UUID (the repository_id in your task snapshot). Omit to write to the repository of the task this run is working on. Anything that is not a UUID is refused — this tool writes, so it does not guess.
